topic: Peasant and Tribal Uprisings of Indian History
description: During British rule, oppressive land revenue policies, strict forest laws, and exploitation by outsiders led to numerous uprisings by peasants and tribal communities. These movements form a crucial, grassroots component of the broader Indian Freedom Struggle.

sections.title: Main Causes of Uprisings
sections.description: The primary economic, social, and administrative factors that triggered widespread tribal and agrarian unrest.

key_concepts.explanation: The introduction of Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari systems imposed exorbitant tax burdens on peasants, often leading to massive debt and the alienation of their land.
A term used by tribal communities (especially in the Chhotanagpur plateau) to describe exploiting outsiders, including moneylenders, traders, contractors, and British revenue officials.
British legislation that restricted traditional tribal rights over forest produce and banned the practice of shifting cultivation (Jhum), severely impacting their livelihood.

sections.title: Major Tribal Uprisings
sections.description: Prominent armed rebellions led by tribal communities against the British Empire and external exploiters.

historical_events.significance: A rebellion by the Bhumij tribes of Midnapore (Bengal) triggered by devastating famine conditions and enhanced land revenue demands.
A massive uprising in the Rajmahal Hills led by brothers Sidhu and Kanhu against oppressive Zamindars and moneylenders. It resulted in the creation of a separate 'Santhal Pargana'.
Led by Birsa Munda in Chhotanagpur to defend the 'Khuntkatti' (joint land ownership) system. It eventually led to the passing of the Chhotanagpur Tenancy Act in 1908.
Initiated by Jatra Bhagat in Chhotanagpur, it started as a socio-religious reform movement among the Oraon tribe but soon acquired an anti-British, political character.

sections.title: Peasant Movements of the 19th Century
sections.description: Major agrarian movements organized primarily against the tyranny of Zamindars, planters, and British economic policies.

historical_events.significance: A highly successful peasant strike in Bengal against forced indigo cultivation by European planters; prominently led by Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas.
A movement in Bengal focused on legal resistance by peasants against the extortionate rent demands and arbitrary evictions practiced by Zamindars.
An uprising by peasants in the Ryotwari areas of Maharashtra, specifically targeting the extreme exploitation and debt traps set by Marwari and Gujarati moneylenders.

sections.title: Peasant Movements of the 20th Century
sections.description: Modern peasant struggles that eventually intertwined with the mainstream Indian National Movement.

historical_events.significance: Mahatma Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in India, organized in Bihar against the oppressive 'Tinkathia' system (growing indigo on 3/20th of the land).
A movement in Gujarat against strict tax collection despite severe crop failure. It marked the rise of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel as a mass leader.
A violent uprising by Muslim tenants (Moplahs) in Kerala against high-caste Hindu landlords (Jenmis) and the British administration.
A highly successful no-tax movement in Gujarat against a 22% hike in land revenue. Vallabhbhai Patel was given the title 'Sardar' by the women of Bardoli during this struggle.
A powerful movement led by the Kisan Sabha in Bengal, demanding that sharecroppers (Bargadars) retain a two-thirds (Tebhaga) share of the harvest instead of half.

sections.title: Important Literature, Organizations, and Leaders
sections.description: Crucial books, organizations, and key figures associated with the peasant and tribal uprisings.

key_associations.extra_info: A famous play that powerfully depicted the immense suffering and exploitation of farmers during the Indigo Revolt.
A renowned novel based on the Sanyasi Rebellion (1763-1800) in Bengal. It features India's national song, 'Vande Mataram'.
Established in Lucknow, it became the largest and most influential national organization advocating for peasant rights in India.
A major tribal guerrilla war fought against the British in the Manyam forest area of the Godavari Agency in Andhra Pradesh.

important_facts.fact: As a direct result of the Deccan Riots, the British government passed the 'Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act' in 1879 to provide protection to farmers against moneylenders.
The Eka Movement (1921), heavily active in Uttar Pradesh and led by Madari Pasi, primarily demanded the conversion of produce rent into cash payment.
